analysis:
## Technical analysis

### Session overview — FOMC fade; third consecutive declining reference close

Bitcoin's 20:00 UTC reference candle closed at $63,522.17 on 2026-07-29 (Crypto.com 1h candle, verified). Reference candle: open $63,604.27 / high $63,744.08 / low $63,366.73 / close $63,522.17 / volume 121.98 BTC ($7.75M). The session decline: −$391.51 / −0.61% from the July 28 reference of $63,913.68.

### Reference close progression — Three consecutive declines

| Session | Reference close | Distance from $65,000 | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| July 27 | $64,957.30 | −$42.70 | peak of ascending pattern |
| July 28 | $63,913.68 | −$1,086.32 | CLARITY Act + Asian crash |
| July 29 | $63,522.17 | −$1,477.83 | FOMC hawkish fade |

The ascending pattern (July 24–27) has been replaced by a descending pattern (July 27-29). The step-aside gap has widened in three consecutive sessions: $43 → $1,086 → $1,478.

### FOMC session narrative — Buy the announcement, sell the press conference

**Pre-FOMC accumulation (00:00–17:00 UTC):** BTC rose from $63,956 (00:00 open) to $64,753 (09:00 UTC session high) on pre-FOMC optimism. The Asian and European sessions sustained $64,400–$64,700 on moderate volume (avg 32–89 BTC/hr). Participants positioned for a dovish hold with cut guidance — the ideal BTC re-entry scenario.

**FOMC announcement + initial reaction (18:00 UTC):** Decision released at 18:00 UTC (2:00 PM ET). The 18:00 UTC candle: open $63,805.98, high $64,295.39, low $63,707.10, close $64,274.07, volume 280.56 BTC — the heaviest candle of the day. Initial market read: 'Fed held, not hawkish' → BTC rallied.

**Press conference fade (19:00 UTC):** The 19:00 UTC candle extended the rally: high $64,666.21, close $64,497.50, volume 204.75 BTC. This was peak post-FOMC optimism.

**Sharp reversal (20:00 UTC reference):** The 20:00 UTC reference candle opened at $63,604.27 — a gap of $893 below the 19:00 close of $64,497.50. This is the FOMC fade: Warsh's press conference hawkish tone (inflation emphasis, three dissents explicitly noted, no cut guidance) caused rapid reversal. Reference close: $63,522.17. Total FOMC fade: $64,666 → $63,522 = −$1,144 / −1.72% peak to reference.

### Volume — FOMC candles confirm session significance

| Period | Volume | Context |
|---|---|---|
| 00:00–12:00 | ~540 BTC | Pre-FOMC accumulation |
| 12:00–16:00 | ~486 BTC | US open / positioning |
| 18:00 UTC | 280.56 BTC | FOMC announcement — heaviest |
| 19:00 UTC | 204.75 BTC | FOMC continuation — second heaviest |
| 20:00 UTC ref | 121.98 BTC | FOMC fade |
| 21:00 UTC | 85.93 BTC | Continued decline |

The two FOMC candles (18:00 + 19:00: 485 BTC combined) represent the session's defining volume block. The fade candle (20:00: 121 BTC) is lighter than the spike candles but still elevated vs the average. This pattern (heavy volume on spike, lighter on fade) is consistent with institutional long entries on the FOMC announcement that were subsequently caught by the press conference reversal.

### Trend — Three-session descending reference pattern; $65,000 resistance strengthening

Six consecutive reference closes below $65,000 (July 24–29) with today's session spending the most time below $65,000. The $65,000 level has been tested intraday (July 27 high $65,739.31, July 29 high $64,753.24) but never achieved on a reference close. The resistance is strengthening — each failed close adds to the wall of supply at $65,000.

### Strongest support — $62,726.80 (July 28 session low)

The V-recovery origin from July 28 remains the strongest support. A retest of $62,726 on continued ETF outflows and elevated September hike odds would be the key test: if buyers defend $62,726 again on a second test, the double-bottom pattern strengthens the floor; if $62,726 fails, $62,000 is the next meaningful level.

### Strongest resistance — $65,000 (six-session reference close rejection)

Six consecutive reference closes below $65,000 has established this as the primary resistance. The FOMC (the primary catalyst expected to breach this level) has failed to deliver. Next catalysts: July 31 options expiry (max pain $64,000, not $65,000), August CPI, and potential CLARITY Act pathway post-recess. The gap is $1,478 — a 2.3% move required.

### Options expiry mechanics — July 31 max pain $64,000

Tomorrow's July 31 expiry carries $9.61B notional OI with max pain at $64,000. Options market makers delta-hedge toward max pain going into expiry — this creates upward gravitational pull of approximately $478 from today's close. The effect is real but limited: max-pain settle at $64,000 closes the step-aside gap to $1,000, not $0. Options expiry alone cannot trigger framework re-entry.

### What invalidates the bear read

A reference close above $65,000 with confirmed net-positive ETF inflows on the same session. The earliest catalyst pathway: July 31 expiry mechanics push BTC above $64,500 → buying momentum spills over to $65,000 → ETF managers see price recovery and reverse outflows. This sequence requires each step to work and is not the base case. A more realistic pathway: August CPI below 2.5% (cutting September hike odds) → risk appetite returns → ETF inflows resume → $65,000 reference close achievable within 1-2 sessions of the CPI print.
